newsitem.title: ALBANIA: German helicopters evacuate Westerners in Albania.
newsitem.headline: German helicopters evacuate Westerners in Albania.

text.p: German helicopters have begun airlifting about 120 foreigners, mainly European Union nationals wishing to escape the unrest in Albania, out of the capital Tirana, a diplomatic source said on Friday.
The source said up to six helicopters had flown to Albania to pick up the foreigners after road transport out of the capital was deemed too dangerous.
The source said the helicopters had landed at an old airfield about two km (one mile) from the German embassy.

"The operation is under way. I understand one helicopter has already gone," the source said. "We felt any evacuation by road was simply too dangerous. We are not sure where the evacuees will go but we have a number of options."

He said a convoy of vehicles organised by the Greek embassy had left Tirana in the morning for the port of Durres, 40 km (25 miles) away and would be taken further by sea. A land convoy organised by Britain left on Thursday.
Italian and U.S. helicopters have been picking up Westerners in Tirana since Thursday.
